column1: That's the date to watch.
Will Kakinada be strong enough by then?
Or will the shield get extended?
And here's the balance the government has to strike.
Protect the Indian plant... without making your antibiotics costlier.
And it's not just penicillin.
Companies have already put more than five thousand crore rupees into this scheme.
And there's more coming.
Three giant bulk drug parks are being built — in Gujarat, in Himachal Pradesh... and one at Nakkapalli.
Yes, you heard right — that's in Andhra Pradesh too, the same state as the Kakinada plant.
Let me be honest with you.
None of those parks is up and running yet.
And China has a thirty-year head start, and makes far more penicillin than we do.
So has India won?
Not yet.
But it's back in the fight.
So here's the lesson.
If you only master the last step, you're only as strong as whoever controls the step before.
And the cost?
You saw it in the Corona days.
When one province in China shut down, the pharmacy of the world had to lock its own doors.
But here's the reality today.
India has the scientists.
It has the factories.
And now, it's growing its own penicillin again.
So what does this mean for you?
Keep taking your medicines exactly as your doctor says.
Nothing in this story changes that.
But the next time you take an antibiotic, think about that white powder.
There's a fair chance part of its journey began in China.
And if the plant in Kakinada wins... the next one might start right here in India.
